title: I built an AI mod maker for Fallout 2. You describe what you want, and it builds a playable mod.
author: theplushpairing
selftext:
I’ve been working on something that combines two things I love: classic RPGs and AI-assisted development.

Fallout 2 came out in 1998, and while it still has an active modding community, creating mods traditionally requires learning a bunch of specialized tools and game-specific systems. Back in the day I was literally changing bits in hex editors and praying the game didn’t crash. 

So I built **RerunReactor**, a tool that exposes Fallout 2 modding capabilities to AI assistants through MCP.

The idea is simple: instead of manually writing scripts and editing game files, you describe what you want to create, and the AI uses the available tools to build it.

You can check it out at [https://www.rerunreactor.com](http://rerunreactor.com)  
I’d love feedback from anyone experimenting with AI agents, procedural content generation, or AI-assisted game development.

If you want to try the MCP you can here — https://rerunreactor.com/mcp

**What would you try building first?**

comments.author: CubersumGame
comments.body: What with the fallout community edition? What the difference?

replies.author: theplushpairing
replies.body:
Based on it yes. It works in any browser, has android/iphone overlays and tap assistants so it’s easier to play. It has a save editor, 50 save slots instead of 10, 3 rotating autosaves, and now this mod maker. 

You can use your steam or gog or any other copy of the game to play.

replies.author: CubersumGame
replies.body: I mean, all of this was already there. What exactly is your contribution? I’m trying to figure out if there’s anything at all on this site that wasn’t already present within the broader modding community.

replies.author: theplushpairing
replies.body: Oh fallout CE just was native mac or pc. This is web assembly working on any browser, so that’s all new. The expanded save slots are all new. The autosave feature is new. The save editor is new and actually a lot more detailed than anything ever done before (companion inventories are editable as well as a much better system of explaining all the global variables and how those affect quests). The mod maker is all new. The mobile phone touch and assisted touch controls are all new. Hope that helps
